evidence.gaps:
The web-search budget, shared by all agents in this run, ran out on the first press-specific query; only 3 searches ran before that. As a result I could not sweep Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, FT or trade press for 2015-2025 coverage. The only press and aggregator items gathered are for 2024 and 2026: Finance Magnates, GuruFocus/Yahoo and Wikipedia. Since Virtu is an SEC registrant, press PnL figures should only restate its releases, so I built the dataset directly from primary filings. That covers 8-K earnings exhibits for all 46 quarters, Q1 2015 through Q2 2026, plus 10-Ks, proxies, and the KCG and ITG 10-Ks. All 69 SEC URLs were checked and return HTTP 200.

Remaining gaps:
(1) There is no exact 2017-12-31 or 2018-12-31 headcount. The only snapshots are ~560 on 2018-03-05 and ~483 on 2019-02-07, and the 2018/2019 proxies have no pay-ratio data. So 2017 and 2018 average headcount is estimated, with wide bars.
(2) There is no official mid-2026 headcount. The 10-Qs give none, so the latest is ~1,027 on 2026-02-13.
(3) Q3 2026 results are not yet released; they are scheduled for 2026-11-05 before market open, per the GlobeNewswire notice of 2026-10-07. The 2026 YTD cutoff is therefore 2026-06-30, H1 2026.
(4) Contractors are not disclosed. Temporary employees (8-14) are inside the 2019-2022 pay-ratio populations.
(5) No average-headcount disclosure exists, so averages are approximated from year-end and early-following-year snapshots.
(6) ANTI for the acquired KCG and ITG before their acquisitions is not included. That is a scope change, not a gap in Virtu's own series.
evidence.red_flags:
(1) The orchestrator lead 'ANTI ranging roughly $0.6B to $2.6B' is WRONG. Actual FY ANTI runs from $414M/$424M (2016) to $2,271M (2020). 2026 is running at about $3.0B annualized ($1,504M in H1). The headcount lead (~150 in 2015, ~1,000 post-ITG) is correct: 148 and ~1,010-1,065.

(2) Definition change. Starting with the Q3 2017 release (post-KCG), ANTI adds commissions/technology services and deducts payments for order flow. 2015 and 2016 were first reported as $500.7M and $414.1M, then restated to $511.3M and $424.5M. Q1 and Q2 2017 were reported as $79.4M and $74.0M, then restated to $82.2M and $77.1M. Mixing vintages understates early years by about 2%.

(3) Restatements and revisions:
- FY2017 net income: $33.3M in the 2018-02-08 release, $18.9M in the 10-K.
- FY2017 GAAP revenues: $1,023.9M, later $1,028.0M.
- FY2019 GAAP revenues: $1,530.1M, recast to $1,517.5M.
- FY2016 net income: $158.5M, then $158.3M.
- FY2020 ANTI: $2,271.4M, then $2,271.3M.

(4) GAAP total revenues are much larger than ANTI, by $0.28B in 2015 and up to $1.49B in 2025, because they are gross of brokerage/exchange/clearance fees, PFOF and interest. Do not use revenues as PnL. FY2017 GAAP revenues also include ~$88M in 'Other, net', mostly the BondPoint sale gain, which ANTI excludes.

(5) Wikipedia's 2024 'net income $276.4M' is net income available to Class A common stockholders; consolidated net income was $534.5M. Its '969 employees (2025)' is the February 2025 snapshot, not end-2025 (1,010).

(6) GuruFocus/Yahoo headlines 'Record Adjusted Net Trading Income' for Q2 2026. The record is trailing-twelve-month; Q2 2026 ($717.9M) was below Q1 2026 ($786.5M).

(7) The Q4 2018 preliminary range ($285-298M) was beaten by the actual ($299.2M). Preliminary flashes (Jan-2020 month: $100-105M) are unaudited.

(8) The July 2026 term loan was marketed at $400M (8-K of 2026-07-14) and closed at $500M (8-K of 2026-07-23). Press figures differ for that reason.

(9) Entity traps:
- Virtus Investment Partners' 'Investor Presentation September 2026' showed up in search results and is a different company.
- Virtu changed its listing from NASDAQ to NYSE in 2025 (8-K 3.01, 2025-05-29), so sources label the ticker differently.
- Virtu Financial LLC is the operating subsidiary; its figures are the same as the consolidated Inc. figures.

(10) Scope changes:
- 2017 includes KCG only from 2017-07-20. KCG had 952 employees at YE2016.
- 2019 includes ITG only from 2019-03-01. ITG had 883 staff at YE2018.
These mid-year jumps distort year-average PnL per head in 2017 and 2019.

(11) The 2019 net loss (-$103.7M) and the 2018 net income spike ($620M, with Q1 2018 alone at $410M) show that GAAP net income is a poor PnL proxy here; ANTI is cleaner.

draft.pnl_definition:
PnL is Adjusted Net Trading Income (ANTI), Virtu's own non-GAAP measure, in USD millions by calendar year. It uses the current definition, introduced with the KCG deal in 2017-18: trading income, net + commissions, net and technology services + interest and dividends income, minus brokerage, exchange, clearance fees and payments for order flow, minus interest and dividends expense. It excludes 'Other, net' items such as the TRA remeasurement, business-sale gains (BondPoint, RFQ-hub) and investment gains.

2015 and 2016 use the restated values from the FY2017 10-K and Q4 2017 release ($511.3M and $424.5M). They were first reported as $500.7M and $414.1M under the older definition, which left out technology services and did not deduct PFOF.

ANTI is net revenue after variable trading costs. It is not profit: it is before compensation, communications, D&A, financing costs and taxes. It also includes the agency commissions earned by Execution Services, which comes from KCG and ITG.

GAAP total revenues and GAAP consolidated net income (including noncontrolling interests, as audited in the 10-K) are given in the notes, and net income in net_income_usd_m.
draft.headcount_definition:
Headcount is the time-weighted AVERAGE number of employees in the calendar year (for 2026, over 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30). It covers all functions and offices and excludes contractors, which Virtu never discloses. The averages are interpolated from primary snapshots:
- 10-K Item 1 counts are 'approximately N employees, all full-time'. From FY2017 onward they are dated February or March of the following year.
- Proxy CEO pay-ratio populations are dated Dec 31 (2019-2025). They include 8-14 temporary employees in 2019-2022.
- 2015 quarterly earnings releases and the November 2015 prospectus also give counts.

For 2017 and 2019 the averages are weighted by days before and after the acquisition close: KCG on 2017-07-20 and ITG on 2019-03-01. This matches the scope of ANTI, which includes each acquired business only from its close. Year-end counts are given in each row's notes.
draft.fx_note: No FX conversion was needed. Virtu Financial Inc. reports in USD, and every PnL, revenue and net income figure is taken directly from USD-denominated SEC filings. The orchestrator's EURUSD and GBPUSD tables were not used.

ANTI, GAAP revenues and net income for every year come from Virtu's SEC filings (CIK 1592386): the Q4 and full-year earnings-release reconciliation tables, the 10-Ks, the 2026 10-Qs and the Q1 and Q2 2026 releases. - KCG's last count (923 on 2017-03-31) and ITG's (883 on 2018-12-31);
- DOL Form 5500 US 401(k) active-participant counts.

caveats: ANTI is a non-GAAP net revenue measure, not profit. It is before compensation ($85M-$528M a year), communications, D&A, interest on corporate debt and taxes. Its Execution Services part includes agency commissions, so it is not pure proprietary trading PnL. Compare PnL per head with peers using a gross or net trading revenue measure, not net profit.

The ANTI definition changed after the KCG deal: commissions and technology services were added and PFOF is deducted. 2015-2016 use the restated values ($511.3M and $424.5M; first reported $500.7M and $414.1M). Mixing the two vintages creates a spurious ~2% break.

There are scope breaks. KCG is included only from 2017-07-20 and ITG only from 2019-03-01, and pre-acquisition results of the acquired firms are excluded. Pre-2017 Virtu was a 148-person pure market maker. From 2019 it is a roughly 1,000-person firm that includes an agency execution business with many sales and support staff. PnL per head is therefore not like-for-like across eras.

2017 and 2018 headcounts are derived. No Dec-31 count was disclosed: Virtu was an emerging growth company with no pay-ratio data. The YE2017 figure (about 650) is triangulated from US-only Form 5500 401(k) participant counts. The 2017 average (about 450) depends on how front-loaded the KCG cuts were; using year-end counts instead of averages would change 2017 and 2019 PnL per head substantially.

Headcount snapshots differ in timing and scope. 10-K counts are dated February or March of the following year and are full-time only. Proxy pay-ratio counts are at Dec 31 and include 8-14 temporary staff in 2019-2022. All annual figures are interpolated averages. Contractors are never disclosed.

2026 covers H1 only (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30). Its headcount (about 1,040) is an estimate, because there has been no disclosure after 2026-02-13. Do not compare H1 PnL per head directly with full years; naive annualization gives about a $3.0B run-rate, but H2 is unknown.

GAAP total revenues are much larger than ANTI and should not be used as PnL. They are gross of brokerage, exchange and clearance fees, PFOF and interest expense, and are inflated by $460-510M a year of interest income in 2023-2025. They also include one-off 'Other, net' items: the 2017 TRA remeasurement of about $86.6M, about $340M of 2018 business-sale gains, and the $67.0M RFQ-hub gain in 2025.

GAAP net income here is consolidated including noncontrolling interests (the Virtu Financial LLC unitholders). Net income attributable to Class A holders is roughly half; for example, 2024 was $276.4M versus $534.5M. FY2017 net income was revised from $33.3M (release) to $18.9M (10-K).
The orchestrator's lead of 'ANTI roughly $0.6B-$2.6B' was wrong: actual ANTI ranges from $424.5M (2016) to $2,271.4M (2020). The headcount lead (~150 rising to ~1,000) was correct.

The research lenses ran out of web-search budget, so independent press corroboration is thin: Finance Magnates, GuruFocus and Wikipedia only restate the filings. For an SEC registrant the primary filings are authoritative, and the synthesizer re-verified the Q2 2026 release and the EDGAR 8-K index directly.
open_questions: Q3 2026 results (quarter ending 2026-09-30) would extend the 2026 YTD cutoff to 2026-09-30. They had not been filed as of 2026-10-08; one lens reports a 2026-11-05 release date, unverified. Re-pull ANTI from that release when it lands.

Actual 2017-12-31 and 2018-12-31 headcounts, and the post-KCG integration path, would shrink the widest headcount bars (2017: 380-540). Possible sources are 2017-2018 earnings-call transcripts, investor-day decks, 10-Q MD&A or FINRA/regulatory filings of the broker-dealer subsidiaries.

The intra-2019 headcount path after the ITG close (how fast the roughly 1,366 combined staff were cut to 1,065 by year-end) would tighten the 2019 average (990-1,140). Earnings-call commentary and synergy disclosures are the likely sources.

A mid-2026 headcount, from Q2 or Q3 2026 earnings-call remarks, LinkedIn employee-count trends, or ultimately the FY2026 10-K due around February 2027, would firm up the 2026 denominator. The FY2025 10-K signals headcount growth.
